Azuki Bean Soup

Served at: Dondoyaki Bonfire

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 45 min

Azuki Bean Soup, also known as "Oshiruko" or "Zenzai," is a traditional sweet red bean soup commonly enjoyed during the Dondoyaki Bonfire festival in Japan. This comforting dish is served to warm up participants as they gather around the bonfire, symbolizing good fortune and the cleansing of the past year's misfortunes.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (200g) dried azuki beans
  • 5 cups (1.2 L) water
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
  • Pinch of salt
  • 4 mochi cakes, toasted or grilled

Method

  1. Rinse the azuki beans under cold water and drain.
  2. Place the beans in a pot with 5 cups of water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
  3. Boil the beans for 5 minutes, then drain the water to remove bitterness.
  4. Return the beans to the pot and add 5 cups of fresh water.
  5. Simmer the beans gently for 40 minutes or until they are soft but not falling apart.
  6. Add the sugar and a pinch of salt to the pot, stirring until dissolved.
  7. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to blend the flavors.
  8. Toast or grill the mochi cakes until puffed and lightly browned.
  9. Ladle the hot azuki bean soup into bowls and add one toasted mochi cake to each bowl before serving.

Tips

  • For a smoother soup, mash some of the beans before adding sugar.
  • Adjust the sweetness by adding more or less sugar to taste.
  • Instead of mochi, you can serve the soup with shiratama dango (rice flour dumplings) for variation.
